latin.150: Atque sic per consequens, August. Confess. Socii quoque indubii sunt Marchiones & Electores Brandenburgici, à GEORGII, Marchionis ac Confess. August. Subsignatoris, & JOACHIMI SECUNDI, Electoris Brandenburgici, & Confessionis Augustanae in regiones suas Introductoris usque tempore, non obstante; quod DIVUS JOHANNES SIGISMUNDUS gloriosissimae memoriae, AUGUSTISSIMI REGIS NOSTRI Proavus, cum Successoribus suis inque omne aevum, per Dei gratiam, secuturis olim, Friderici Palatini interpretationem August. Confess. quoad Articulum X., unà cum Theologis suis non impugnaverit;
latin.151: Cùm ceterà, tàm ipse Joh. Sigismundus, quàm ejus Successores, tum semetipsos Declarationibus variis, tùm Theologos suos, per Statuta etiam Facultatis Theologicae Francofurtensis, solenni juramento, ad August. Conf. Carolo V. Anno 1530. exhibitam, ac deinceps prolixius expositam, ceu ad praecipuum Regionum Brandenburgicarum Librum Symbolicum, seriò severéque obligaverint, totóque pectore addixerint. Vid. Joh. Crocium Comment. de A. C. Societate parte 1. integra, à pag. 1. ad 30.;
latin.152: Ut hinc etiam Lutheranae Ecclesiae haud incelebris hodieque Antecessor Consistoriiique S. Sambiensis Regiomonti Borussorum Assessor, nunc etiam quartus in ordine, Theologiae Professor Ordinar. Christianus Waltherus, de Facultatis nostrae Juramento certior factus, quô post Sacram. Scripturam, solis quatuor Conciliis Oecumenicis & Augustanae Confessioni ceu Symbolicis Scriptis perpetuò nos adhaesuros, solenniter recipimus, abhinc annis duobus, Theologiae Doctoris Gradum à Facultate nostra Theologica petere nullus dubitaverit, etiam eôdem, post praestitum subsignatumque Juramentum, jussu PIENTISSIMI REGIS NOSTRI, à dicta Facultate, per me, eo tempore Decanum, mactatus sit, prout fusius id refert Significatio, nomine Facultatis Theologicae Viadrinae, Anno 1702. typis evulgata. Tam Juramentum Facultatis nostrae, quam Mandatum Regium, utpote clementissimum, & Promovendi pariter Lutherani, atque Promoventium Reformatorum conatibus faventissime applaudens, non abs re fuerit, hôc locô subjunxisse. Juramentum hisce conceptum verbis est &c.
latin.153: Ego Magister Christianus Walther juro, me sanam Doctrinam Evangelii Christi & verbi Prophetarum & Apostolorum, cujus capita in tribus Symbolis & Confessione, Carolo V. Augustae exhibita, comprehensa & explicata habentur, ut rectè cognitam ita diligenter & fideliter custoditam traditurum ac defensurum; Omnia falsa, Heretica & cum manifesto Dei verbo pugnantia, tam veterum quàm novorum Arrianorum, & aliorum Fanaticorum hominum Dogmata sedulò ac pro virili declinaturum impugnaturumque esse:
latin.154:
De iis, qui ad gradus Theologicos sunt admittendi, severè judicaturum & graviter pronunciaturum, hunc Gradum nullibi repetiturum & omnia quae ad Ecclesiae Dei utilitatem, ad Gloriam Christi, & ad hanc Facultatem atque Scholam juvandam, ornandam atque augendam, videbuntur spectare, summa fide & perpetuo studio facturum esse; Sic me Deus adjuvet per sanctum suum Verbum.
Juramentum suprà scriptum me fideliter servaturum, tam nominis mei subscriptione, quàm appresso Sigillo meo sancte attestor atque polliceor, d. 15. Aprilis Anno 1702.
(L. S.)
M. Christianus Walther,
Pastor Sackheimensis, Consistorii Sambiensis Assessor, & Societatis Scientiarum Brandenburgicae membrum, manu suâ.
latin.155:
Rescriptum vero Regium ita sonat:
FRIDERICUS, D. G. REX BORUSSIAE,
Marchio Brandenburgensis, S. R. J. ArchiCamerarius & Princeps Elector, Magdeburgi, Cliviae, Juliae, Montium, Stetini, Pomeraniae &c. Dux &c.
Reverendi, Doctissimi, Dilecti ac Fideles;
Etsi jam antehac perspecta nobis sit M. Christiani Waltheri, Pastoris Sackheimensis Regiomonti Borussorum, haud vulgaribus elogiis à vobis commendati, singularis Eruditio, morum probitas juxta & vitae integritas, Nosque de meritis ejus affatim edoctissimi, adeò, ut vel ex hac sola ratione, illum exoptatis honoribus neutiquam destitutum censeamus; Magis tamen nos incitavit, ut votis ipsius, vestrisque humillimis annueremus precibus, rarissimum hactenus Theologi Lutherani exemplum, Docturam Theologicam à Reformatae fidei Doctoribus non minori fiducia expetentis, quàm horum in promovendis ejus desideriis est promptitudo & reciprocum studium. Non potest non Nobis hoc esse gratissimum, cùm salutaria quaevis ac prospera Rei, tàm Publicae, quàm Ecclesiasticae, inde ominari liceat. Consentimus itaque non solùm, verùm mandamus etiam Tibi, Samueli Strimesio, Facultatis Theologicae Decano, nec non Doctori & Professori Ordinario, ut & Pastori Ecclesiae Primario, ut praefatum M. Christianum Waltherum, nunc quidem in Facultate Vestra, S. S. Theologiae Doctorem declares, in proximo verò Promotionis publicae futuro Actu, talem publicè proclames & renuncies, omniumque Privilegiorum ac Jurium, summo huic Axiomati annexorum, ac Doctoribus Theologiae per S. R. J. competentium, participem reddas, quod Divinum Numen secundare dignetur. valete, de Gratia Nostra Regia securi. Dabantur Coloniae ad Svevum d. 20. Martii. Ao. 1702.

FRIDERICUS REX.

PAULUS, LIB. BARO de FUCHS.
Ad Facultatem Theologicam Universitatis Viadrinae.

pass_a.150: And so consequently, the Margraves and Electors of Brandenburg are also undoubted Associates of the Augsburg Confession, from GEORGE, Margrave and Subscriber of the Augsburg Confession, and JOACHIM THE SECOND, Elector of Brandenburg and Introducer of the Augsburg Confession into his territories, down to this time — notwithstanding that the DIVINE JOHN SIGISMUND of most glorious memory, Great-grandfather of OUR MOST AUGUST KING, with his Successors and those hereafter to follow through all ages by God's grace, did not impugn Frederick the Palatine's interpretation of the Augsburg Confession as to Article X, together with his Theologians;
pass_a.151: Since for the rest, both Johann Sigismund himself and his Successors have seriously and severely bound, and with whole breast devoted, now themselves by various Declarations, now their Theologians, also through the Statutes of the Theological Faculty of Frankfurt, by solemn oath, to the Augsburg Confession exhibited to Charles V in the Year 1530 and thereafter more fully expounded, as to the chief Symbolic Book of the Brandenburg Regions. See Joh. Crocius, Comment on the Society of the A.C., part 1 entire, from p. 1 to 30;
pass_a.152: So that hence also Christian Walther, still today a not obscure Predecessor of the Lutheran Church and Assessor of the Holy Sambian Consistory at Königsberg in Prussia, now also fourth in order Ordinary Professor of Theology, having been made more certain concerning our Faculty's Oath — by which after Holy Scripture we solemnly receive that we will perpetually adhere to the four Ecumenical Councils alone and to the Augsburg Confession as Symbolic Writings — two years ago did not hesitate at all to seek the Degree of Doctor of Theology from our Theological Faculty, and even by the same, after the Oath had been performed and signed, by command of OUR MOST PIOUS KING, was decorated by the said Faculty through me, then Dean, as the Signification published in type in the Year 1702 in the name of the Viadrina Theological Faculty more fully reports. It will not be beside the point to have subjoined in this place both our Faculty's Oath and the Royal Mandate, as being most clement and most favorably applauding the endeavors alike of the Lutheran being promoted and of the Reformed promoters. The Oath is conceived in these words, &c.
pass_a.153: I, Master Christian Walther, swear that I will hand on and defend the sound Doctrine of the Gospel of Christ and of the word of the Prophets and Apostles — whose heads are held comprehended and explained in the three Symbols and in the Confession exhibited to Charles V at Augsburg — as rightly known, so diligently and faithfully kept; that I will carefully and according to my strength decline and impugn all false, Heretical dogmas and those fighting with the manifest word of God, of both the old and the new Arians, and of other Fanatical men:
pass_a.154: Concerning those who are to be admitted to Theological degrees, that I will judge severely and pronounce gravely; that I will nowhere repeat this Degree; and that I will do with highest faith and perpetual zeal all things that will seem to look to the utility of the Church of God, to the Glory of Christ, and to helping, adorning, and increasing this Faculty and School; So help me God through His holy Word. That I will faithfully keep the Oath written above I holy attest and promise both by subscription of my name and by my Seal pressed on, the 15th day of April in the Year 1702. (L. S.) M. Christian Walther, Pastor of Sackheim, Assessor of the Sambian Consistory, and member of the Brandenburg Society of Sciences, with his own hand.
pass_a.155: But the Royal Rescript sounds thus: FREDERICK, by the Grace of God KING OF PRUSSIA, Margrave of Brandenburg, Arch-Chamberlain of the Holy Roman Empire and Prince Elector, Duke of Magdeburg, Cleves, Julich, Berg, Stettin, Pomerania, and so on. Reverend, Most Learned, Beloved and Faithful; Although the singular Erudition of M. Christian Walther, Pastor of Sackheim at Konigsberg in Prussia, recommended by you with no common praises, and the uprightness of his morals together with integrity of life, have already before this been clear to us, and We have been abundantly taught concerning his merits, so that even from this reason alone we would judge him by no means destitute of the honors desired; yet more has the rarest example thus far of a Lutheran Theologian seeking Theological Doctorate from Doctors of the Reformed faith with no less confidence than is their readiness and reciprocal zeal in promoting his desires incited us to assent to his vows and to your most humble prayers. This cannot but be most grateful to Us, since any wholesome and prosperous things for the Public as for the Ecclesiastical Commonwealth may thence be omened. We therefore not only Consent, but also command You, Samuel Strimesius, Dean of the Theological Faculty, and also Doctor and Ordinary Professor, and Primary Pastor of the Church, that you declare the aforesaid M. Christian Walther now indeed in Your Faculty Doctor of Sacred Theology, and in the next future Act of public Promotion proclaim and announce him such publicly, and make him partaker of all Privileges and Rights annexed to this highest title and belonging to Doctors of Theology through the Holy Roman Empire, which the Divine Numen may deign to second. Farewell, secure of Our Royal Grace. Given at Cologne on the Spree, the 20th day of March, Year 1702. FREDERICK THE KING. PAULUS, Freiherr de FUCHS. To the Theological Faculty of the Viadrina University.

150: Consequently the Brandenburg Margraves and Electors are likewise undoubted Augsburg Confession associates — from George (Margrave and AC subscriber) and Joachim II (Elector who brought the Confession into his lands) down to our day.

That holds even though blessed Johann Sigismund of glorious memory — great-grandfather of our most august King — with his successors forever after, by God's grace, did not attack Frederick the Palatine's reading of AC Art. X, nor did his theologians.
151: For the rest, Johann Sigismund and his successors have bound themselves by various declarations, and their theologians through the Frankfurt theological faculty statutes, by solemn oath, to the Augsburg Confession shown to Charles V in 1530 and later more fully set out — as the chief symbolic book of the Brandenburg lands — and have devoted themselves to it with their whole heart.
See Crocius, Comment on A.C. Society, part 1 entire, pp. 1–30.
152: Hence also Christian Walther — still a well-known Lutheran churchman, Assessor of the Holy Sambian Consistory at Königsberg in Prussia, and now fourth Ordinary Professor of Theology — once informed of our faculty oath (that after Holy Scripture we solemnly bind ourselves forever to the four ecumenical councils alone and to the Augsburg Confession as symbolic writings) did not hesitate two years ago to seek a doctorate of theology from our faculty.

After he took and signed the oath, by command of our most pious King the faculty decorated him through me (then Dean), as the 1702 printed Signification in the Viadrina theological faculty's name reports more fully.

It is not out of place here to add both our faculty oath and the royal mandate — most gracious, and warmly favoring the efforts of the Lutheran candidate and of the Reformed promoters alike. The oath runs in these words, &c.
153: I, Master Christian Walther, swear that I will hand on and defend the sound doctrine of Christ's Gospel and of the Prophets' and Apostles' word — whose chief points are contained and explained in the three Symbols and in the Confession shown to Charles V at Augsburg — knowing it rightly and keeping it diligently and faithfully.
I will carefully and as far as I can refuse and attack all false and heretical dogmas that fight the clear word of God, whether of old or new Arians or of other fanatics.
154: As to those admitted to theological degrees, I will judge strictly and speak with weight; I will not take this degree over again elsewhere; and with highest faithfulness and constant zeal I will do whatever seems to serve God's church, Christ's glory, and the help, honor, and growth of this faculty and school. So help me God through His holy Word.
I holy attest and promise that I will keep the oath written above, both by signing my name and by affixing my seal, 15 April 1702.
(L.S.) M. Christian Walther, Pastor of Sackheim, Assessor of the Sambian Consistory, and member of the Brandenburg Society of Sciences — in his own hand.
155: The royal rescript runs thus: Frederick, by God's grace King of Prussia, Margrave of Brandenburg, Arch-Chamberlain of the Holy Roman Empire and Prince Elector, Duke of Magdeburg, Cleves, Julich, Berg, Stettin, Pomerania, and so on.

Reverend, most learned, beloved and faithful: Walther's uncommon learning, upright manners, and integrity of life — praised by you without ordinary compliments — were already clear to us, and we know his merits well enough that on that ground alone we would not leave him without the honors he seeks.

What moved us still more to grant his wish and your humble petitions is this rare case: a Lutheran theologian seeking a theological doctorate from Reformed doctors with as much confidence as they show readiness and mutual zeal in advancing his desire.

That can only please us, since every wholesome good for the commonwealth and the church may be hoped from it. We therefore not only consent but command you, Samuel Strimesius — dean of the theological faculty, ordinary doctor and professor, and primary pastor — to declare M. Christian Walther now Doctor of Sacred Theology in your faculty, and at the next public promotion to proclaim him such, and to admit him to all privileges and rights belonging to that highest title and to doctors of theology in the Holy Roman Empire — which may God favor. Farewell, secure of our royal grace. Given at Cologne on the Spree, 20 March 1702.
Frederick the King. Paul, Freiherr von Fuchs. To the Theological Faculty of the Viadrina University.
